title: motion-strip's W4 hash net misindexes against the manifest for any demo with a pause: strip collects per-STEPPED-tick hashes, manifest records per-WALL-tick hashes (paused ticks included) — false 'STATE DIVERGENCE' on a green timeline (reproduced)
evidence: motion_strip.odin:140-153: `paused := paused_at(cfg.pauses[:], w, hz)` / `if !paused {` / `sim_tick += 1` / `before := len(state.events)` / ... / `append(&hashes, pp.state_hash(&state, state.events[before:], cat, context.temp_allocator))` — no hash appended for paused wall ticks. run.odin:399-406: `before := len(state.events)` / `paused := paused_at(cfg.pauses[:], w, hz)` / `if paused {` / `// paused: no step, no event drain — the hash MUST equal the` / `// window baseline (state stable)...` / `append(&hashes, pp.state_hash(&state, state.events[before:], cat, context.temp_allocator))` — one manifest hash per WALL tick. check_manifest_prefix compares `hashes[i] != m.hashes[i]` index-by-index (harness/manifest.odin:192-197). Live repro at this sha: `./bin/harness run pause` → 'PASS pause ticks=2000 / harness: 1 demo(s) green'; `./bin/harness motion-strip pause 95000 99000 17 /tmp/mp-pause-test` → 'motion-strip: T1 drift — T1: STATE DIVERGENCE at tick 1211: 568780a239c47780 != golden 09bbc05e1b830b64' + exit 2 (pause.dem pauses at 60500ms: manifest[1210..1399] are the 190 paused stable hashes the strip skips).
detail: Any demo whose pause schedule precedes the strip window end shifts the strip's hash list against the manifest's wall-tick list; the verb false-fails with a misleading divergence claim on a timeline the golden gate proves identical.
recommended_fix: Match run_demo's convention: append the paused-tick stable hash (events[before:] is empty there) for paused wall ticks in motion_strip, so strip hashes align 1:1 with manifest wall-tick indices.

title: The W4 drift check runs AFTER every frame is exported — 'refusing to emit a strip from a divergent timeline' is false; the full strip is written to disk before exit 2 (reproduced: 236 PNGs emitted)
evidence: Inside the walk loop, motion_strip.odin:184: `if !render_strip_frame(rc, &state, outdir, demo_name, t, sim_tick, alpha, &frames) {` (render_strip_frame calls `rl.ExportImage(img, ...)` and writes `%s/%s-%06dms.png`). Only after the loop, motion_strip.odin:204-211: `if len(hashes) > 0 {` / `fails: [dynamic]string` / `defer delete(fails)` / `check_manifest_prefix(demo_name, &demo, cat.hash, hz, hashes[:], &fails)` / `if len(fails) > 0 {` / ... / `fmt.eprintln("motion-strip: refusing to emit a strip from a divergent timeline (re-bless deliberately)")` / `return 2`. Live repro: `./bin/harness motion-strip pause 95000 99000 17 /tmp/mp-pause-test` exited 2 with the refusal message AND `ls /tmp/mp-pause-test | wc -l` = 236 frame PNGs already on disk.
detail: On a true divergence the misleading strip fully lands on disk despite the refusal claim; any consumer of the outdir (script globbing, a reviewer) gets unvetted evidence with no failure marker.
recommended_fix: Verify each tick's hash against the manifest prefix incrementally inside the loop (fail before rendering that tick's frames), or buffer frames in memory and write the outdir only after the prefix check passes.

title: [still present since r3] The 'delivery snap' pin still doesn't isolate delivery — interp_continuous now reads p.delivered, but the test's assertion passes via the anchor mismatch with the delivered branch removed
evidence: motion_test.odin:209-218: `// delivery: the packet vanished (delivered=true)...` / `p: pp.Packet` / `motion_test_packet(&p)` / `p.delivered = true` / `// a delivered packet's anchor is irrelevant...` / `p.on_edge = false` / `p.at_node = 2` / `testing.expect(t, !interp_continuous(&topo, 0, 1, 0, true, &p), "delivered transition must snap")`. Entry anchor is (on_edge=true, edge=0, heading=1); without the delivered check the arrival branch evaluates `entry_heading(1) == p.at_node(2)` → false → still snaps. view.odin:176-179: `if p.delivered {` / `return false` / `}` — the code half of W3 landed, but the r3 prescription 'a test with at_node == heading' was not delivered, so deleting the delivered branch leaves the pin green.
detail: The pin cannot detect removal of the delivered guard; r3 W3's test-isolation half is unfixed (production remains safe — draw_packets skips delivered packets before interp).
recommended_fix: Set the test packet to an arrival-continuous anchor (entry_heading == p.at_node, e.g. at_node=1 with entry (on_edge,edge=0,heading=1)) so only the delivered flag forces the snap.

title: measure_packet_motion.py exits 0 when zero frames track in both strips — a wrong BODY color or degenerate --xmax (0/negative) degrades every frame to 'lost' with no failure signal (r3 N11 residual)
evidence: tools/measure_packet_motion.py:167-172: `b_lost = sum(1 for _, d in before if d is None)` / `a_lost = sum(1 for _, d in after if d is None)` / ... / `print(f"lost track (packet absent): BEFORE={b_lost}  AFTER={a_lost}")` — then 184: `return 0` unconditionally. `live_centroid` scans `for x in range(min(xmax, img.width)):` so `--xmax 0` or a negative value yields an empty scan (all lost); a mis-set BODY/PP_MEASURE_BODY does the same.
detail: The Rule-4 evidence pipeline can go fully vacuous (0 tracked frames) while exiting success; scripts consuming the exit code propagate empty evidence as green.
recommended_fix: Exit non-zero when not a single frame tracked in either strip (e.g. `if b_lost == len(before) and len(before) > 0: return 2`), and reject --xmax <= 0 at parse.
